verdict.rationale: Apple's own AI stack documents support for M5's GPU Neural Accelerators and Neural Engine. MLX explicitly supports Metal 4 and the GPU Neural Accelerators, Metal 4 Tensor APIs program the Neural Accelerators directly, and Core ML, Metal Performance Shaders and Foundation Models benefit automatically, with PyTorch backends and LM Studio also noted. Missing for 10: no evidence of llama.cpp or ONNX Runtime support documentation, and no independent or hands-on corroboration of runtime support on M5.

support.subject: As a developer, mainstream local-AI runtimes target this silicon — llama.cpp, MLX, ONNX Runtime, or the vendor's own AI software stack document support for its CPU, GPU, or NPU

citations.quote: MLX is an open-source array framework that lets you experiment with, training, researching, and fine-tuning generative models on Apple Silicon. It supports Metal 4 and GPU Neural Accelerators for maximum performance
Developers can also build solutions for their apps by directly programming the Neural Accelerators using Tensor APIs in Metal 4.
Applications using built-in Apple frameworks and APIs — like Core ML, Metal Performance Shaders, and Metal 4 — can automatically see immediate increases in performance.
The Neural Accelerators on M5 increase performance for GPU-based AI workloads running on device within apps like LM Studio.
